solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Knocked, but the sound is absorbed

indicators.note: the sound is tells us to take a word as it is said aloud, not as written

parts.note: someone absorbed in a book is rapt

explanation.surface: Someone knocked at a door, but the noise was muffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapped is the past tense of rap, to strike with sharp blows, so it is a synonym of knocked.

definitions.meaning: Daphne du Maurier's novel bears this woman's name
in Genesis the wife of Isaac bore Esau and Jacob

explanation.definitionFit: This is both the title of du Maurier's famous novel and a form of the name of Isaac's wife in the Bible.

parts.note: a pine is one kind of tree
an apple is another kind of tree

explanation.surface: Someone harvests a fruit that seems to come from a pair of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineapple is a tropical fruit with spiky skin and sweet yellow flesh.

parts.note: still and even both intensify, as in still better or even better

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: O's are ring shapes, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone keeps telephoning regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so is an idiom meaning despite that, the same as nevertheless.

clue.text: When retired, Edward longed to be free of ties

indicators.note: retired is read as drawn back, so the short name is written backwards

parts.note: Ted is a short form of the name Edward
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A man called Edward looks forward to retirement and freedom from obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When retired' makes the short name read backwards; 'longed' looks like part of a sentimental retiree's story but is just a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detached is separate and unconnected, without the ties that bind it to anything else.

clue.text: Tender put up for capital statue

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a sore spot is tender to the touch

explanation.surface: A tender is offered for work on a monument in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns SORE round. EROS is the popular name of the statue at Piccadilly Circus, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged figure in Piccadilly Circus, London, is popularly known by the Greek love god's name.

clue.text: How one may seem to be lying, eventually

definitions.text: How one may seem to be lying
definitions.meaning: stretched out full length, as someone lying down is

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both stretched out fully and in the end, after much time.

parts.note: a hip is the fruit of the rose
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A creature comes upon fruit lying on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts HIP above PO.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippo, short for hippopotamus, is a large African animal.

clue.text: Side playing away from home fails to survive

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of the word are moved around in play

parts.note: taken as written
someone out is not at home

explanation.surface: A team playing an away match is knocked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dies out becomes extinct, failing to survive.

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
Ned Kelly was the famous Australian bushranger

explanation.surface: Barred, the outlaw Ned Kelly sits in his cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlaw' reads as a noun beside Kelly, but it is the verb BAN; Ned Kelly was a nineteenth-century Australian outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Banned and barred both mean prohibited or excluded by rule.

clue.text: Firm left to slip into bankruptcy

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm
a lapse is a slip or small error

explanation.surface: A company's small errors cause it to slide into insolvency.
explanation.definitionFit: A business collapse is its financial failure, which is what bankruptcy amounts to.

indicators.note: we hear means what is said aloud, not what is written

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: A bill presented to a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a bill listing charges owed, as with a restaurant account.

clue.text: Study group is occupied by a number of great literary works

parts.note: a class is a group of pupils studying together

indicators.note: something occupied by another has it inside, so the word is holds the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A study group fills its time reading great books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is occupied by' sounds like a classroom being taken over, but it tells the solver to put the Roman hundred inside the word is.
explanation.definitionFit: The classics are the established great works of literature, especially of Greece and Rome.

parts.note: the Latin phrase for wholly or altogether is what the clue asks for

explanation.definitionFit: This Latin expression means entirely or as a whole, used in English unchanged.

clue.text: A fault in a fool or comic

indicators.note: in places the fault inside the fool

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a fool
a sin is a moral fault

explanation.surface: Folly in a fool or a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the moral failing within the dupe; the second 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amusing is funny, which is what comic means as an adjective.

clue.text: Current assertion of private secretary status

parts.note: saying I am something is an assertion of what you are
PS is the abbreviation for a private secretary

explanation.surface: A civil servant asserts their standing as a private secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assertion of ... status' is someone saying 'I AM PS'; the letters AM and PS join.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric current is measured in units of this name, so they stand for current here.

definitions.meaning: a pledge or undertaking to do something
dedication or devotion to a cause or person

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a pledge given and steadfast dedication to something.

clue.text: Look! He is taken in by girl — fluttering them?

parts.note: to eye is to look at

indicators.note: taken in by means the first piece is held inside the second

parts.note: lass is a girl, a Scottish and northern English word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Look, a man is captivated by a girl batting her lashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' sounds like a man being fooled by a girl, but it means held inside her; the question mark flags the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: What a flirtatious girl flutters are the hairs fringing her eyelids.

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quietly
resumed means started again, carried on

explanation.surface: Things carried on quietly, as anticipated.
explanation.definitionFit: What is presumed is assumed or taken for granted in advance, so expected.

indicators.note: to break the letters is to split them up and reassemble them in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rallying call for geeks to rise up and liven things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks like the definition's verb, but it shuffles NERDS ARISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreariness is dull sameness, the quality of being tedious, which is monotony.

parts.note: golf clubs called by the same name as motorists, read as clubs that drive

explanation.definitionFit: Long golf clubs used off the tee share their name with people who drive cars.

parts.note: S for south, one of the four compass quarters
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: A broadcaster transmits coverage of a quarter-final match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter-final' looks like one sporting word but splits into quarter (S) and final (END); 'broadcast of' extends the definition's sense of sending out.
explanation.definitionFit: To send a signal or message is to transmit it.

clue.text: A title in fact much wished for

indicators.note: in places the title within the word for fact

parts.note: a deed is a fact or act, as in in deed meaning in fact
Sir is the title given to a knight

explanation.surface: A knighthood is in fact greatly coveted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the knight's title inside the word for an act; in deed is an old way of saying in fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Something desired is strongly wanted, much wished for.

parts.note: to age is to mature

indicators.note: moving means these letters shift around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mature and touching programme.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items or plans to be dealt with, a programme.

parts.note: in stands for into here
a vest is an undergarment worn beneath a shirt (British usage)

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs cash into their underclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: A VEST in Britain is a sleeveless undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest is to put money into something in the hope of a return.

definitions.meaning: in Twelfth Night Duke Orsino comes to love the heroine disguised as Cesario
a stringed instrument slightly larger than the violin

explanation.definitionFit: This is both Shakespeare's heroine whom Orsino loves and the alto member of the violin family.

clue.text: They make the grandee enraged or angered

definitions.text: They make the grandee enraged or angered

parts.words: They make the grandee enraged or angered
parts.note: rearranging the letters of grandee gives both enraged and angered, so these are what turn the noble furious

explanation.definitionFit: Words formed by rearranging another word's letters, as enraged and angered are of grandee.

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, and his contented vibrating sound is meant

explanation.definitionFit: The low vibrating sound a contented cat makes is the vibe of a happy tom.

clue.text: Extra-large portion of chicken or moussaka

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone orders a huge helping of either the chicken or the moussaka.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means very large indeed, the same as extra-large.

clue.text: It could get Charon in a fix on the Styx

definitions.text: It could get Charon in a fix on the Styx

indicators.note: in a fix means in trouble, so the letters of the ferryman's name are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Charon, ferryman of the dead, might find himself in difficulty on the river Styx.
explanation.walkthrough: Charon ferried souls across the Styx in Greek myth; what fixes his boat in place is a rearrangement of his own name.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy weight dropped to hold a boat in position, fixing it on the water.

definitions.meaning: a flag, which soldiers call the colours

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the normal level of something and a military flag or banner.

parts.note: the word for brought up also means lifted high, so a child reared is a child lifted

explanation.definitionFit: Children are raised when they are bred or brought up, and things are raised when lifted high.
